hints: Look carefully at the last column first. How many haem groups does one haemoglobin have, and what does 50% saturation mean for that number?
Recall what a haem group really is. Is it made of amino acids, or is it a non-protein prosthetic group containing iron?
walkthrough:
**Recall the big picture of haemoglobin**

Think of haemoglobin as a classic globular protein with quaternary structure. It is made of four polypeptide chains, two alpha and two beta, folded into an almost spherical shape.

Key rule:
$$1 \text{ haemoglobin} = 4 \text{ chains} = 4 \text{ haem groups} = 4 \text{ O}_2 \text{ molecules max}$$

**Check oxygen numbers and haem chemistry**

Each haem group holds one $Fe^{2+}$ iron ion, and each iron ion binds one $O_2$ molecule reversibly to form oxyhaemoglobin. So full saturation is four $O_2$ molecules, and 50% saturation is two $O_2$ molecules.

Calculation:
$$50\% \text{ of } 4 = 2 \text{ oxygen molecules}$$

**Spot the trap statements**

Haem is not a group of amino acids, it is a prosthetic (non-protein) group surrounding iron. Also, hydrophobic R-groups point inward to the centre to keep the globular shape stable in water, they do not surround the iron ion. Only row A gets all four ideas right.

options.A: All four statements are correct. Four chains each with haem, iron binds oxygen reversibly, hydrophobic groups face inward, and 50% of 4 sites means 2 O2 molecules carried.
options.B: Contains two errors. It says globular chain instead of globular protein, and wrongly describes haem as a group of amino acids when haem is a prosthetic group.
options.C: First three columns are true, but the last is false. One molecule carries four oxygen molecules, which is eight oxygen atoms, not four oxygen atoms.
options.D: Contains two errors. Haemoglobin is globular, not a loose helix, and hydrophobic R-groups point to the centre of the chain, they do not surround the iron ion.
